title: What does XLS-66 specify for Lending?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-66 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-66 describes the XRPL lending protocol's brokers, loans and first-loss-cover lifecycle. [1]

The proposal defines distinct operations for creating loans, making payments, managing impairment or default and handling broker cover. Inspect its dependencies and network support before assuming the transaction family is usable. A protocol representation of a credit agreement does not eliminate borrower default, liquidity, underwriting or legal risk; these remain relevant even when accounting transitions validate correctly. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-66 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Draft. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-66 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
